entities.title: Points for each alien
entities.summary: Each kind of alien scores its own points, more when shot diving, and a diving queen more for each escort shot first.
entities.statement: Shot (or rammed) in the hive, a queen scores 60, a guard 50, a drone 40 and a worker 30. Diving, a guard scores 100, a drone 80 and a worker 60, and a queen 200, or 400 or 800 if one or two of the escorts on her dive were shot first.
entities.rationale: The README gives players these numbers, and the title screen shows them.
acceptanceCriteria: A worker shot at home scores 30; a guard shot diving scores 100.
A diving queen with none, one or two escorts shot first scores 200, 400 or 800.
A diving alien that rams the ship destroys both and still scores.

origin.description: Hivestorm's README, written for players and developers (Rules).

entities.title: Ships, waves and the swarm
entities.summary: Three ships and one extra at 7,000; each wave harder; the last five aliens never go home.
entities.statement: A player starts with 3 ships and gets one extra ship at 7,000 points. Clearing the hive starts the next wave, which dives faster and more often with more aliens out at once. When only 5 aliens are left they stop going home and dive one after another. A queen may dive with up to two guards from beside her.
acceptanceCriteria: Clearing the hive raises the wave and brings back all 37 aliens.

origin.description: Hivestorm's README, written for players and developers (Rules).

entities.title: Scores can't be faked
entities.summary: A score on the table is only ever what the server's replay of the game computed.
entities.statement: The server issues each game's seed, replays the recorded controls with the same engine before listing any score, and accepts each seed once.
entities.rationale: A public table is only worth climbing if nobody can type a score into it.
acceptanceCriteria: Controls that do not play exactly one whole game are refused.
A game with a different number of players than names is refused.

origin.description: Hivestorm's README, written for players and developers (How scores are checked).

entities.title: Friends play on their own devices, taking turns
entities.summary: Two players can play each other online, each on their own computer, phone or tablet, as they would take turns on one machine.
entities.statement: An online game started from the multiplayer page is played by two signed-in players on two devices, who see exactly the same two-player game. Each plays their own turns with their own controls and watches the other's; if one leaves, the other plays both turns. Each can put their own score on the table. There is no two-player game on one device.

origin.description: Hivestorm's README, written for players and developers (Playing online).

entities.title: Playing needs a sign-in
entities.summary: The game and its score API are for players signed in to icelander.net; the table stays public.
entities.statement: The game's page, a new game's seed and a score submission need a sign-in to icelander.net with the games:play role. The table, as JSON or as a page, needs none.

origin.description: The repository README: every game needs icelander.net's sign-in; the high-score tables stay public.

entities.title: Keys or touch
entities.summary: The game can be played with a keyboard or with buttons on a touch screen.
entities.statement: 1 or PLAY starts a game; ← → (or A D) or ◀ ▶ move; Space (or ↑, Ctrl, Enter) or FIRE fire, held to keep firing; P or Esc or PAUSE pauses; M or SOUND turns the sound on or off.

origin.description: Hivestorm's README, written for players and developers (Playing).

entities.title: Only a name is stored
entities.summary: A score is stored with a name of up to 12 characters, and nothing else about the player.
entities.statement: The table stores a name of up to 12 plain characters with each score, with the wave reached and how many played. No email address or other personal data is asked for or kept.

origin.description: Hivestorm's README, written for players and developers (Rules, High scores).

entities.title: An original game
entities.summary: Hivestorm copies none of the formation-and-dive shooters it follows: its name, creatures, art, sounds, text, scoring numbers and code are its own.
entities.statement: Hivestorm belongs to the formation-and-dive shooter genre of the late 1970s but takes no name, creature, pixel art, sound, screen text, scoring number or code from any title in it.

origin.description: Hivestorm's README, written for players and developers.
